item.text: I’ll use Fructal Cap Design to inspect the fixture and propose a recovery flow that preserves the submission through a timeout.

**Acknowledge receipt as soon as the service has safely recorded the title and all selected files.** The receipt should say “Received — scan pending,” show the request ID, and let the submitter return to their original location. The required scan still gates completion. A receipt confirms that the service has the documents, without implying they passed.

1. **Preserve the work before sending.** Assign one request ID before the first upload. Keep the title, selected files, upload progress, and return location attached to that ID. Keep the form intact while the outcome is uncertain. At the return location, show a link back to the same request.
2. **Recover from a timeout in place.** Show “Checking receipt” and look up the existing ID. If the service already has the complete submission, show its current status. If it has only part, resume the missing uploads under the same ID. If the lookup also times out, keep the work visible and offer “Check again.” The service must recognize repeated sends under that ID, including a delayed original send, as one submission.
3. **Make the next step clear.** While scanning is pending or temporarily interrupted, the service owns recovery and updates the receipt. On success, mark the request complete. If a file needs replacement, identify it and offer a replacement control beside it. Preserve the title, other files, return location, and request ID, and scan the replacement before completion. Navigating away leaves the request active. An explicit cancellation should report the service-confirmed outcome, including if completion happened first.

**Evidence and open decisions.** The scanning requirement and losses on retry come from your report. The fixture contains only `state=blocked`, so it does not establish the timeout’s cause or what storage is permitted. Confirm where unscanned files may be staged and for how long. If an interruption makes a local file unavailable, retain its name and ask the submitter to reselect only that file.

**Verification plan.** Delay the scan and check that one receipt appears before completion. Interrupt an upload midway, then separately drop the response after the service has accepted every file. Retry each request twice and verify one ID, one submission, the original title and return location, and no repeat upload of confirmed files. Exercise scanner interruption, file replacement, navigation away and back, browser restart, and cancellation racing with completion. Use a keyboard and screen reader to check that status changes are announced, focus stays in place, and recovery controls identify the affected file.

This is a proposal. The fixture was left unchanged, and the proposed paths have not been tested.
